beats.title: Intro: The Jacket Trick
beats.says: A jacket costs £80. The price goes up 20%, then down 20%. So it's back to £80, right? Not quite: it's £76.80. By the end of this video you'll know exactly why, and you'll never get a percentage question wrong again.

beats.title: The Picture: Percent Means Per Hundred
beats.says: Percent means per hundred. Picture the whole price as one bar: that's 100%. Split it into ten equal blocks, and each block is 10%. 10% of £80 is £8.
beats.key: The whole amount is 100%. 10% is a tenth of it.

beats.title: The Picture: Going Up
beats.says: Now increase it by 20%: add two more blocks. The new price is 100% plus 20%, which is 120% of the original. As a decimal, that's 1.2. So £80 times 1.2 is £96.

beats.title: The Method: Going Down
beats.says: Decreases work the same way. Take 15% off, and what's left is 85%. That's 0.85. So £80 times 0.85 is £68. One multiplication, no adding or taking away.

beats.title: The Method: Finding the Multiplier
beats.says: So every percentage change has a multiplier. Up 20% is times 1.2. Up 5% is times 1.05. Down 15% is times 0.85. Down 3% is times 0.97. Start from 100, add or take away, then divide by 100.

beats.title: The Jacket Explained
beats.says: Back to the jacket. Up 20%: £80 times 1.2 is £96. Then down 20%: £96 times 0.8 is £76.80. The 20% off was taken from the bigger price, so it's not back to £80.

beats.title: Reverse Percentages
beats.says: Now the exam favourite. After a 20% rise, a jacket costs £96. What was it before? The trap is taking 20% off £96. But the 20% was of the original price, not this one. £96 is 120% of the original, so undo the multiplier: divide by 1.2. The original price was £80.
beats.key: Reverse percentage? Divide by the multiplier.

beats.title: Compound Interest
beats.says: Compound interest just repeats the multiplier. £1000 in a bank at 5% a year. After one year, £1050. After two, £1102.50. After three years, £1157.63. That's £1000 times 1.05 to the power of 3.
beats.key: Compound interest: multiply by the multiplier once per year.

beats.title: Percentage Change
beats.says: To find a percentage change, divide the change by the original, then times by 100. From £80 to £96 is a change of £16. 16 divided by 80 is 0.2, which is 20%.
beats.onScreen: Worked: change = 96 − 80 = 16 // new − original | 16 ÷ 80 = 0.2 // divide by the ORIGINAL | 0.2 × 100 = 20%

beats.title: Exam Tips: Common Mistakes
beats.says: The mistakes that lose marks: taking the percentage of the new amount in reverse questions, using 1.15 for a 15% decrease, dividing by the new amount for percentage change, and adding the interest only once.
beats.onScreen: Worked: ✗ £96 − 20% // reverse: ÷ 1.2 | ✗ −15% → × 1.15 // it's × 0.85 | ✗ 16 ÷ 96 // divide by the original | ✓ find the multiplier · × or ÷

beats.title: Your Turn: Question
beats.says: Your turn. In a sale, a phone costs £240 after a 20% discount. What was the original price? Pause the video and try it.
beats.onScreen: Your turn: question card with a countdown. Q: After a 20% discount, a phone costs £240. What was the original price?
beats.question: After a 20% discount, a phone costs £240. What was the original price?

beats.title: Your Turn: Answer
beats.says: A 20% discount leaves 80%, so the multiplier is 0.8. It's a reverse percentage, so divide: £240 divided by 0.8 is £300. If you got that, you've got it.
beats.question: After a 20% discount, a phone costs £240. What was the original price?
